summary: A seat's delivery, read and close of graph mail are recorded on its own host as local marks instead of lifecycle claims, once every member reads them (db break-up step 4b, the writers)

replay.detail: Once marks are on, this member writes no message.delivered, message.read or message.closed claim for a seat its own declarations place on it; it records a local mark instead (local_message_marks), which never replicates. A staging is still a message.staged claim: this build reads stagings recorded as marks (local_message_staged), and a later release records them once a release that reads them exists, so a rollback never offers staged mail again. Lifecycle claims already written keep counting, and readers take the further of a message's claims and marks. Persons, seats on other hosts, acted-for retired seats, delegated writes, native Claude-channel reads and delivery-probe mail (tagged delivery-probe, whose senders and doctor prove its read by the replicated claim) still write claims.

schema.detail: New member-local tables local_message_staged and local_message_mark_events, with their triggers; no change to any replicated table. Builds that read local_message_marks ignore both.

rules.detail: Marks are on only while every other current member, and every peer this daemon is configured with, advertises seat_freshness_reads=1, read from each member's own newest daemon.started at its incarnation; ambiguous membership counts as not ready, and a member alone switches at once. The daemon decides it at startup and every minute, and doctor's message-marks check shows the decision and what holds it off. Every 4b-2 build advertises message_offsets=1, so other members ask it on the seat-freshness relay how far its seats got.

compatibility.detail: A member on a release without seat_freshness_reads (v0.3.24 and earlier) keeps every other member writing claims, so it reads lifecycle as before. Members with it (v0.3.25 on) ask a marks-recording host for its seats' mail in delivery status (st conversations status), doctor and the mail-backlog check, and show unknown, never sent, when that host does not answer; their message view and message lists read only their own records, so there a hosted seat's marked mail shows the state of its last replicated claim (sent, or staged) until a later step reads them through the relay too. A member that joins without the feature turns marks off within a minute of its admission reaching this member; until then it shows the seats' mail this member marked in that window as undelivered, and nothing is delivered again because of it. Lifecycle requests (POST /v1/mailbox/receipts, POST /v1/messages/{id}/claims, cleanup, handoff acknowledgement) keep their request shapes; for a hosted seat's delivery, read or close they answer the mark's offset-receipt, whose store_index is 0.

downtime.detail: No migration: the new tables are created empty, and marks start with the next lifecycle write once the barrier holds.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to v0.3.25 or later is safe: it reads the marks, offers nothing again, and writes claims from then on. Rolling back to v0.3.24 or earlier after marks were on shows mail delivered since then as undelivered, and its unread mail is redelivered once. Version 4 backups with marks restore on any release that reads them.
